facts.statement: Spinosaurus was described by Ernst Stromer in 1915.
facts.quote: authority: Stromer, 1915

facts.statement: The type species of Spinosaurus is Spinosaurus aegyptiacus.
facts.quote: type_species: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus

facts.statement: Spinosaurus lived in North Africa during the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 100 to 94 million years ago.
facts.quote: lived in what is now North Africa during the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous period, about 100 to 94 million years ago

facts.statement: Spinosaurus was first discovered in Egypt in 1912 and described by Ernst Stromer in 1915.
facts.quote: The genus was known first from Egyptian remains discovered in 1912 and described by German palaeontologist Ernst Stromer in 1915

facts.statement: A 2022 study suggests Spinosaurus aegyptiacus could have reached 14 meters in length and 7.4 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: A 2022 study suggests that S. aegyptiacus could have reached 14 m in length and 7.4 MT in body mass

facts.statement: Spinosaurus had a long, low, narrow skull similar to a modern crocodilian with straight conical teeth that had few to no serrations.
facts.quote: The skull of Spinosaurus was long, low, and narrow, similar to that of a modern crocodilian, and bore straight conical teeth with few to no serrations

facts.statement: Spinosaurus had distinctive neural spines extending from its vertebrae that grew to at least 1.65 meters long and likely formed a sail-like structure covered in skin.
facts.quote: The distinctive neural spines of Spinosaurus, which were long extensions of the vertebrae, grew to at least 1.65 m long and were likely to have had skin connecting them, forming a sail-like structure

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Spinosaurus was semiaquatic, though the extent of its swimming ability is strongly contested.
facts.quote: Evidence suggests that it was semiaquatic, although the extent of its swimming capability has been strongly contested

facts.statement: Spinosaurus may have first been discovered in October 1898 when Fernand Foureau found two teeth in southern Algeria.
facts.quote: The first discovery of Spinosaurus may have been in October 1898, when French geologist Fernand Foureau unearthed two unusual teeth in Cenomanian-aged sediments of the Djoua Escarpment in what is now southern Algeria

facts.statement: The name Spinosaurus means "spine lizard", derived from Latin and Greek words for spine and lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name Spinosaurus comes from the Latin spina, meaning "spine", and the Greek sauros, meaning "lizard", and thus "spine lizard"

facts.statement: It is unclear whether the fossils represent one or two distinct species of Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: It is unclear whether one or two species are represented in the fossils reported in the scientific literature

facts.statement: The validity of Sigilmassasaurus, S. maroccanus, and Oxalaia as distinct taxa from Spinosaurus is debated.
facts.quote: Possible junior synonyms include Sigilmassasaurus and the dubious S. maroccanus from the Kem Kem beds and Oxalaia from the Alcântara Formation in Brazil, though the distinction and validity of these taxa have been debated

facts.statement: Many studies have proposed that fossils assigned to Spinosaurus or Sigilmassasaurus actually belong to other dinosaur groups like iguanodonts or carcharodontosaurids.
facts.quote: However, much of the anatomy of Spinosaurus still remained obscure and many studies proposed that fossils previously assigned to the genus or Sigilmassasaurus were actually from iguanodont ornithischians, megaraptorans, carcharodontosaurids, or other forms of theropod

facts.statement: Some researchers differentiated Spinosaurus maroccanus from S. aegyptiacus based on the ratio of centrum length to posterior articular facet height in neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: S. maroccanus was differentiated from S. aegyptiacus based on the length of its neck vertebrae.

facts.statement: Later authors debated the validity of S. maroccanus, suggesting vertebrae length varies between individuals.
facts.quote: Later authors have been split on this topic, with some authors noting that the length of the vertebrae can vary from individual to individual

facts.statement: Some studies have referred the holotype and other specimens of S. maroccanus to S. cf. aegyptiacus.
facts.quote: Some studies have referred to the holotype and other referred specimens of S. maroccanus (NMC 50791 and MNHN SAM 124–128) as S. cf. aegyptiacus.

facts.statement: Specimens previously identified as paratypes of S. maroccanus were reidentified as spinosaurids not identifiable at the generic level.
facts.quote: The specimens previously ascribed as paratypes of S. maroccanus (NMC 41768 and NMC 50790) were reidentified as spinosaurid specimens that are currently not identifiable at the generic level.

facts.statement: In 1996, Paul Sereno and colleagues assigned cervical vertebrae of "Spinosaurus B" and Sigilmassasaurus to Carcharodontosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1996, a study by American paleontologist Paul Sereno and colleagues assigned cervical vertebrae referred to "Spinosaurus B" and the spinosaurid Sigilmassasaurus (a possible synonym of Spinosaurus) to the carcharodontosaurid Carcharodontosaurus.

facts.statement: Later analyses proved that "Spinosaurus B" and Sigilmassasaurus are not synonyms and do not contain fossils from Carcharodontosaurus.
facts.quote: however later analyses have proven that "Spinosaurus B" and Sigilmassasaurus are not synonyms or contain fossils from Carcharodontosaurus.

facts.statement: It is still debated whether "Spinosaurus B" should be referred to Sigilmassasaurus.
facts.quote: Some studies have continued to refer "Spinosaurus B" to Sigilmassasaurus, although this is still debated.

facts.statement: In 2008, a Moroccan fossil collector presented fragmentary fossils to Nizar Ibrahim, who suspected they belonged to Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Proposed neotype In 2008, a Moroccan fossil collector based in Erfoud presented a few fragmentary dinosaur fossils to Italian paleontologist Nizar Ibrahim, who suspected they may belong to Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: Nizar Ibrahim identified the MSNM fossils as potentially belonging to Spinosaurus based on similar sandstone matrix and neural spine morphology to Stromer's 1915 depiction.
facts.quote: Ibrahim recognized that the MSNM fossils and the ones he had seen in 2008 were from a similar sandstone matrix and that the neural spines of the MSNM fossils were similar to those depicted by Stromer in 1915, leading him to think that they may be from the same individual and belonged to Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2013, Ibrahim, Samir Zouhri, and David Martill located the original fossil dealer in Casablanca.
facts.quote: In 2013, Ibrahim, Moroccan paleontologist Samir Zouhri, and British paleontologist David Martill ventured to Casablanca in search of the original fossil dealer, who they were able to track down.

facts.statement: A subadult skeleton including skull fragments, vertebrae, neural spines, a sacrum, hindlimbs, pedal phalanges, and dorsal ribs was unearthed over several years.
facts.quote: Over the course of several years, a skeleton of a subadult individual consisting of skull fragments, some cervical, dorsal, and caudal vertebrae, neural spines, a complete sacrum, much of the hindlimbs, several pedal phalanges, and several dorsal ribs was unearthed.

facts.statement: The subadult skeleton comes from the Douria Formation of the Kem Kem Beds in Zrigat, Morocco, dated to the Cenomanian stage of the mid-Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: This skeleton comes from a locality of the Douria Formation of the Kem Kem Beds in Zrigat, Morocco, dated to the Cenomanian stage of the mid-Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The description of the remains was controversial because authors claimed Spinosaurus was possibly quadrupedal, semiaquatic, and short-limbed.
facts.quote: The description of these remains were met with intrigue, surprise, and controversy, as the authors claimed that Spinosaurus was a possibly quadrupedal, semiaquatic, short-limbed spinosaurid.

facts.statement: Multiple paleontologists have demonstrated the specimen is not a chimera and represents a Spinosaurus with much smaller hind limbs than previously thought.
facts.quote: However, it has been demonstrated by multiple paleontologists that the specimen is not a chimera, and is indeed a specimen of Spinosaurus that suggests that the animal had much smaller hind limbs than previously thought.

facts.statement: In 2015, researchers rejected a neotype proposal for specimen FSAC-KK-11888 due to a lack of locality data, geographical separation from the holotype, and anatomical differences.
facts.quote: In 2015, British paleontologist Serjoscha Evers and colleagues rejected the neotype proposal for FSAC-KK-11888 on the basis of the lack of association or locality information for FSAC-KK-11888, the geographical separation between the holotype and FSAC-KK-11888 localities, and anatomical differences between FSAC-KK-11888 and the holotype.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists argue that specimen FSAC-KK-11888 likely belongs to Spinosaurus marrocanus rather than Spinosaurus aegyptiacus.
facts.quote: Evers and colleagues argue for the validity of both S. marrocanus and S. aegyptiacus, stating that FSAC-KK-11888 likely belongs to the former.

facts.statement: Researchers have suggested that specimen FSAC-KK-11888 might be a composite of different individuals or a chimera of two species, or that it does not belong to Spinosaurus at all.
facts.quote: Additionally, some paleontologists have suggested that the proportions of the dorsal vertebrae compared to the legs of FSAC-KK-11888 when compared to the proportions of "Spinosaurus B" illustrate that either the former is a composite (a specimen composed of multiple individuals of the same species)/chimera (a specimen composed of material from two or more species) between an individual known from dorsal vertebrae and an individual known from limb, pelvic, and tail material or that FSAC-KK-11888 is not from Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: Expeditions between 2015 and 2019 uncovered additional fossils of FSAC-KK-11888, including caudal vertebrae making up about 80% of the tail with a preserved length of 4 meters.
facts.quote: Between 2015 and 2019, several additional expeditions to the site unearthed additional fossils of FSAC-KK-11888 including many caudal vertebrae, composing about 80% of the tail with a preserved length of 4 m, elements of the pes and hindlimbs, skull fragments, and more.

facts.statement: Since its discovery, Spinosaurus has been considered a contender for the largest theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Since its discovery, Spinosaurus has been a contender for the largest theropod dinosaur.

facts.statement: In 1926 and 1982, researchers listed Spinosaurus as among the most massive theropods, estimating it at 15 meters in length and over 6 metric tons in weight.
facts.quote: Both Friedrich von Huene in 1926 and Donald F. Glut in 1982 listed it as among the most massive theropods in their surveys, at 15 m in length and upwards of 6 MT in weight.

facts.statement: In 1988, Gregory S. Paul listed Spinosaurus as the longest theropod at 15 meters but estimated its mass at 4 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 1988, Gregory S. Paul also listed it as the longest theropod at 15 m, but gave a lower mass estimate of 4 MT.

facts.statement: In 2005, Dal Sasso and colleagues estimated Spinosaurus was 16 to 18 meters long and weighed 7 to 9 metric tons based on skull length proportions similar to Suchomimus.
facts.quote: In 2005, Dal Sasso and colleagues assumed that Spinosaurus and the related Suchomimus had the same body proportions in relation to their skull lengths, and estimated that Spinosaurus was 16 to 18 m long and weighed 7 to 9 MT.

facts.statement: In 2007, François Therrien and Donald Henderson estimated Spinosaurus body length at 12.6 to 14.3 meters and mass at 12 to 20.9 metric tons based on skull lengths of 1.5 to 1.75 meters.
facts.quote: In their 2007 paper using scaling to extrapolate theropod body size based on skull length, François Therrien and Donald Henderson challenged previous estimates of the size of Spinosaurus. Based on estimated skull lengths of 1.5 to 1.75 m, they estimated a body length of 12.6 to 14.3 m and a body mass of 12 to 20.9 MT

facts.statement: In 2020, researchers suggested caution when using skull length to extrapolate Spinosaurus size because the preorbital region may grow allometrically and under different selection pressures.
facts.quote: In 2020, Nicolás Campione and David Evans suggested to take caution with the approach using skull length for extrapolation, namely that of Spinosaurus, since the preorbital region of some dinosaurs grow allometrically (disproportionately with body size) and the cranial properties were likely under different selection pressures unrelated to body size.

facts.statement: In 2022, Paul Sereno and colleagues suggested Spinosaurus aegyptiacus reached a maximum length of 14 meters and mass of 7.4 metric tons using a CT-based 3D skeletal model.
facts.quote: In 2022, however, Paul Sereno and his colleagues suggested that Spinosaurus aegyptiacus reached a maximum body length of 14 m and a maximum body mass of 7.4 MT by constructing a CT-based 3D skeletal model "with the axial column in neutral pose."

facts.statement: Spinosaurus had a narrow snout containing straight, conical teeth without serrations.
facts.quote: Its skull had a narrow snout filled with straight conical teeth that lacked serrations.

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Spinosaurus had six or seven teeth on each side at the front, followed by twelve teeth in the maxillae behind them.
facts.quote: There were six or seven teeth on each side of the very front of the upper jaw, in the premaxillae, and another twelve in both maxillae behind them.

facts.statement: The tip of the Spinosaurus snout was expanded, and a small crest was located in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: The very tip of the snout holding those few large front teeth was expanded, and a small crest was present in front of the eyes.

facts.statement: Dal Sasso et al. (2005) estimated the adult Spinosaurus skull length at 1.75 meters.
facts.quote: Dal Sasso et al. (2005) estimated that the skull of an adult Spinosaurus was 1.75 m long

facts.statement: Hendrickx et al. (2016) suggested that an adult Spinosaurus skull length of 1.6 meters is more likely.
facts.quote: Hendrickx et al. (2016) suggested that a length of 1.6 m is more likely.

facts.statement: The estimated skull length of the Spinosaurus subadult neotype is up to 1.12 meters.
facts.quote: The estimated skull length of the subadult neotype is up to 1.12 m.

facts.statement: A 2026 study interpreted cranial material from Spinosaurus and related species as evidence of a sensitive neurovascular system and rapid tooth replacement starting at a young age.
facts.quote: A 2026 study analyzed cranial material of two Spinosaurids, including two specimens referred to the controversial species S. maroccanus, their findings were interpreted as indicative of a highly developed, sensitive neurovascular system and a high tooth replacement rate in Spinosaurids from a young age.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus possessed a long, muscular neck curved into an S-shape.
facts.quote: As a spinosaurid, Spinosaurus would have had a long, muscular neck, curved in a sigmoid, or S-shape.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus had prominent shoulders and large, stocky forelimbs with three clawed digits on each hand.
facts.quote: Its shoulders were prominent, and the forelimbs large and stocky, bearing three clawed digits on each hand.

facts.statement: The first finger, or thumb, of Spinosaurus was the largest digit.
facts.quote: The first finger (or "thumb") would have been the largest.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus had long finger bones and only slightly curved claws, indicating hands longer than those of other spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Spinosaurus had long phalanges (finger bones), and only somewhat recurved claws, suggesting that its hands were longer compared to those of other spinosaurids.

facts.statement: Tall neural spines on the back vertebrae formed the structure commonly known as the Spinosaurus sail.
facts.quote: Very tall neural spines growing on the back vertebrae of Spinosaurus formed the basis of what is usually called the animal's "sail".

facts.statement: The neural spines of Spinosaurus were over ten times longer than the diameter of the vertebral bodies they extended from.
facts.quote: The lengths of the neural spines reached over 10 times the diameters of the centra (vertebral bodies) from which they extended.

facts.statement: Stromer (1915) suggested the Spinosaurus back structure was more like a fat hump than a sail.
facts.quote: The structure may also have been more hump-like than sail-like, as noted by Stromer in 1915

facts.statement: Ibrahim and colleagues (2014) posited that the Spinosaurus spines were tightly covered by skin, similar to a crested chameleon.
facts.quote: In 2014, Ibrahim and colleagues instead posited that the spines were covered tightly by skin, similar to a crested chameleon, given their compactness, sharp edges, and likely poor blood flow.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus hind limbs were short, accounting for just over 25 percent of total body length, with the tibia longer than the femur.
facts.quote: The hind limbs were short, at just over 25 percent of the total body length, with the tibia being longer than the femur.

facts.statement: Unlike other theropods, the hallux of Spinosaurus touched the ground and had unusually long, well-built phalanges.
facts.quote: Unlike in other theropods, the hallux (or fourth toe) of Spinosaurus touched the ground, and the phalanges of the toe bones were unusually long and well-built.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus feet had shallow claws with flat bottoms, a morphology seen in shorebirds that suggests adaptation for walking on unstable substrates and possible webbing.
facts.quote: At their ends were shallow claws that had flat bottoms. This type of foot morphology is also seen in shorebirds, indicating that Spinosauruss feet evolved for walking across unstable substrate and that they may have been webbed.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus tail vertebrae projected significantly elongated, thin neural spines, an extreme version of the condition seen in some other spinosaurids.
facts.quote: From the caudal vertebrae of the tail projected significantly elongated, thin neural spines, akin to the condition observed in some other spinosaurids, though to a more extreme degree.

facts.statement: Elongated chevron bones on the underside of the tail combined with neural spines to create a deep, narrow, paddle-like tail comparable to those of newts and crocodilians.
facts.quote: Coupled with the also elongated chevron bones on the underside of the caudals, this resulted in a deep and narrow tail with a paddle or fin-like shape, comparable to the tails of newts and crocodilians.

facts.statement: Ernst Stromer originally named the clade Spinosauridae to include only Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Spinosauridae was a clade named by Stromer for just Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: Some researchers, such as Alfred Romer, proposed that Acrocanthosaurus and Altispinax belonged to Spinosauridae due to their tall neural spines, though later studies rejected this.
facts.quote: However, some studies by paleontologists like American researcher Alfred Romer included the high-spined theropods Acrocanthosaurus and Altispinax in Spinosauridae based on their tall neural spines.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus was first discovered from Egyptian remains found in 1912 and described by German paleontologist Ernst Stromer in 1915.
facts.quote: El género se conoció por primera vez a partir de restos egipcios descubiertos en 1912 y descritos por el paleontólogo alemán Ernst Stromer en 1915.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus lived in what is now northern Africa, specifically Egypt, Morocco, and Niger, during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 100 to 94 million years ago.
facts.quote: Spinosaurus (gr. «lagarto de espinas») es un género de dinosaurios terópodos espinosáuridos grandes que vivieron en lo que ahora es el norte de África durante el Cenomaniano del período Cretácico Superior, hace unos 100 a 94 millones de años, en lo que hoy es Egipto, Marruecos y Níger.

facts.statement: Two valid species of Spinosaurus are currently recognized: S. aegyptiacus and S. mirabilis.
facts.quote: Actualmente se conocen dos especies válidas: S. aegyptiacus (la especie tipo) y S. mirabilis.

facts.statement: A 2022 study suggests that S. aegyptiacus could have reached a length of 14 meters and a mass of 7.4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2022 sugiere que S. aegyptiacus podría haber alcanzado los 14 m (46 pies) de longitud y 7,4 t (8,2 toneladas cortas) de masa corporal.

facts.statement: The Spinosaurus skull was long, low, and narrow, similar to a modern crocodile, and possessed straight conical teeth with little to no serration.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Spinosaurus era largo, bajo y estrecho, similar al de un cocodrilo moderno , y tenía dientes cónicos rectos con pocas o ninguna serración .

facts.statement: Spinosaurus had distinctive neural spines extending from its vertebrae that grew to at least 1.65 meters long and were likely connected by skin to form a sail-like structure.
facts.quote: Las distintivas espinas neurales de Spinosaurus , que eran largas extensiones de las vértebras , crecieron hasta al menos 1,65 m (5,4 pies) de largo y es probable que tuvieran piel que las conectaba, formando una estructura similar a una vela .

facts.statement: Spinosaurus is known to have fed on both aquatic and terrestrial prey.
facts.quote: Se sabe que Spinosaurus se alimentaba tanto de presas acuáticas como terrestres.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Spinosaurus was semi-aquatic, although the extent of its swimming ability has been heavily debated.
facts.quote: La evidencia sugiere que era semiacuático , aunque el alcance de su capacidad natatoria ha sido muy cuestionado.

facts.statement: Multiple functions have been proposed for the dorsal sail of Spinosaurus, including thermoregulation and display to intimidate rivals or attract mates.
facts.quote: Se han propuesto múltiples funciones para la vela dorsal, incluyendo la termorregulación y la exhibición , ya sea para intimidar a sus rivales o para atraer parejas.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus lived in a wet environment of marshes and mangroves alongside other dinosaurs, as well as fish, crocodylomorphs, lizards, turtles, pterosaurs, and plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: Vivía en un entorno húmedo de marismas y manglares junto a muchos otros dinosaurios, así como peces, crocodilomorfos, escamosos, tortugas, pterosaurios y plesiosaurios.

facts.statement: Research by Marcos Sales and colleagues in 2017 suggests that South American spinosaurids like Angaturama, Irritator, and Oxalaia were intermediate between Baryonychinae and Spinosaurinae, indicating that Baryonychinae may be non-monophyletic.
facts.quote: research by Brazilian paleontologist Marcos Sales and colleagues (2017) indicate that the South American spinosaurids Angaturama, Irritator, and Oxalaia were intermediate between Baronychinae and Spinosaurinae based on their craniodental features and cladistic analysis.

facts.statement: It is unclear whether one or two species are represented in the fossil record reported in the scientific literature.
facts.quote: No está claro si una o dos especies están representadas en los fósiles reportados en la literatura científica.

facts.statement: The first discovery of Spinosaurus may have occurred in October 1898 when French geologist Fernand Foureau unearthed two unusual teeth in Cenomanian sediments at the Djoua escarpment in what is now southern Algeria.
facts.quote: El primer descubrimiento de Spinosaurus pudo haber ocurrido en octubre de 1898, cuando el geólogo francés Fernand Foureau desenterró dos dientes inusuales en sedimentos del Cenomaniense de la escarpa de Djoua, en lo que hoy es el sur de Argelia

facts.statement: In 1905, French geologist Émile Haug described fossils unearthed during the expedition, including two teeth he assigned to the fish Saurocephalus.
facts.quote: En 1905, el geólogo francés Émile Haug describió los fósiles desenterrados durante la expedición, incluyendo los dos dientes que asignó al pez Saurocephalus.

facts.statement: However, in 1915, German paleontologist and Spinosaurus describer Ernst Stromer reassigned the teeth to Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1915, el paleontólogo alemán y descriptor de Spinosaurus, Ernst Stromer, reasignó los dientes a Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: The first Spinosaurus remains that can be identified with certainty were discovered in the autumn of 1912 by Austro-Hungarian paleontologist Richard Markgraf.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Spinosaurus que se pueden identificar con certeza fueron descubiertos en el otoño de 1912 por el paleontólogo austrohúngaro Richard Markgraf

facts.statement: In 1915, Stromer described these remains as belonging to a new genus and species of dinosaur, Spinosaurus aegyptiacus.
facts.quote: En 1915, Stromer describió estos restos como pertenecientes a un nuevo género y especie de dinosaurio, Spinosaurus aegyptiacus.

facts.statement: The generic name Spinosaurus comes from the Latin spina, meaning "spine", and the Greek sauros, meaning "lizard", and therefore "spiny lizard".
facts.quote: El nombre genérico Spinosaurus proviene del latín spina, que significa "espina", y del griego sauros, que significa "lagarto", y por lo tanto "lagarto espinoso".

facts.statement: The specific name aegyptiacus derives from Egypt, where the fossils were unearthed.
facts.quote: El nombre específico aegyptiacus deriva de Egipto, donde se desenterraron los fósiles.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Spinosaurus aegyptiacus (BSP 1912 VIII 19) consists of jaw elements (lower jaw), a fragment of the maxilla (upper jaw), cervical (neck), caudal (tail), and dorsal (back) vertebrae, including most of the neural spines, ribs, teeth, and some gastralia (belly ribs).
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de Spinosaurus aegyptiacus (BSP 1912 VIII 19) consta de elementos de la mandíbula (mandíbula inferior), un fragmento de maxilar (mandíbula superior), vértebras cervicales (cuello), caudales (cola) y dorsales (espalda), incluyendo gran parte de las espinas neurales, costillas, dientes y algunas gastralias (costillas del vientre).

facts.statement: In April 1914, another expedition to the Bahariya oasis, led by Markgraf, unearthed an incomplete skeleton (BSP 1922 X45) of a spinosaurid.
facts.quote: En abril de 1914, otra expedición al oasis de Bahariya, dirigida por Markgraf, desenterró un esqueleto incompleto (BSP 1922 X45) de un espinosáurido.

facts.statement: After much deliberation due to the war and tense Anglo-German relations, the skeleton arrived in Germany in 1922, where it was described by Stromer in 1934.
facts.quote: Tras muchas deliberaciones debido a la guerra y las tensas relaciones anglo-alemanas, el esqueleto llegó a Alemania en 1922, donde fue descrito por Stromer en 1934.

facts.statement: Stromer assigned the skeleton to Spinosaurus but considered it sufficiently different from S. aegyptiacus to belong to its own Spinosaurus species, "Spinosaurus B".
facts.quote: Stromer asignó el esqueleto a Spinosaurus , pero lo consideró lo suficientemente diferente de S. aegyptiacus como para pertenecer a su propia especie de Spinosaurus, "Spinosaurus B".

facts.statement: Unfortunately, during the night of April 24 to 25, 1944, the building of the Paläontologisches Museum München (Bavarian State Collection of Palaeontology) of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences suffered severe damage during the British bombing of Munich.
facts.quote: Desafortunadamente, durante la noche del 24 al 25 de abril de 1944, el edificio del Paläontologisches Museum München (Colección Estatal Bávara de Paleontología) de la Academia Bávara de Ciencias sufrió graves daños durante el bombardeo británico de Múnich.

facts.statement: Due to personal and political tensions between Stromer and the museum curator, a fervent Nazi, the Spinosaurus fossils stored there were not relocated and were subsequently destroyed as a consequence of the bombing.
facts.quote: Debido a las tensiones personales y políticas entre Stromer y el curador del museo, un ferviente nazi, los fósiles de Spinosaurus que allí se conservaban no fueron reubicados y posteriormente destruidos como consecuencia del bombardeo.

facts.statement: In 1995, Stromer's son donated his father's archives to the Paläontologische Staatssammlung München, leading to a 2006 study by American researcher Joshua Smith and colleagues on photographs, two of which corresponded to the Spinosaurus holotype.
facts.quote: En 1995, el hijo de Stromer donó los archivos de su padre a la Paläontologische Staatssammlung München, lo que dio lugar a un estudio en 2006 realizado por el investigador estadounidense Joshua Smith y sus colegas sobre las fotografías, dos de las cuales correspondían al holotipo del Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: Spinosauridae has been the subject of numerous phylogenetic analyses, commonly finding Spinosaurus in a clade with spinosaurids such as Irritator and Oxalaia.
facts.quote: Spinosauridae ha sido objeto de numerosos análisis filogenéticos, encontrándose comúnmente a Spinosaurus en un clado con espinosáuridos como Irritator y Oxalaia

facts.statement: However, research by Brazilian paleontologist Marcos Sales and colleagues (2017) indicates that South American spinosaurids Angaturama, Irritator, and Oxalaia were intermediates between Baryonychinae and Spinosaurinae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la investigación del paleontólogo brasileño Marcos Sales y sus colegas (2017) indica que los espinosáuridos sudamericanos Angaturama , Irritator y Oxalaia eran intermedios entre Baronychinae y Spinosaurinae

facts.statement: This suggests that Baryonychinae might not be monophyletic and that Spinosaurinae is reduced, including only Angaturama, Spinosaurus, and Oxalaia.
facts.quote: Esto sugiere que Baryonychinae podría no ser monofilético y que Spinosaurinae está reducido, incluyendo únicamente a Angaturama, Spinosaurus y Oxalaia.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis conducted by Barker and colleagues (2021) separated Spinosaurus specimens into their own OTUs (Operational Taxonomic Units; a group of organisms under phylogenetic study), finding Sigilmassasaurus, several referred Spinosaurus specimens, and the Spinosaurus holotype in a clade.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético realizado por Barker y colegas (2021) separó los especímenes de Spinosaurus en sus propias OTU (Unidades Taxonómicas Operativas; un grupo de organismos bajo estudio filogenético), encontrando a Sigilmassasaurus, varios especímenes referidos de Spinosaurus y el holotipo de Spinosaurus en un clado.

facts.statement: Within this clade, the Spinosaurus holotype and the proposed neotype (FSAC-KK 11888) are sister taxa.
facts.quote: Dentro de este clado, el holotipo de Spinosaurus y el neotipo propuesto (FSAC-KK 11888) son taxones hermanos.

facts.statement: The parent group of Spinosaurus is Spinosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Spinosaurini
